statement: The algebra R in Proposition 2.1 is the first algebra A0 of a sequence (Aj)j≥0 with the following properties. There are positive integers c, k, h0, D, with D > 10(c + 1)(k + 1), and hj = h0Dj , Lj = 2 · 2hj + 1. 3 For each j ≥ 0: (i) Aj is presented by a finite alphabet Σj, finitely many replacements, and finitely many zero declarations, all of length at most k. It is graded by word length. (ii) There is a substitution Ej sending each letter of Σj+1 to a word of length Lj over Σj. Extended by concatenation, it induces a unital algebra homomorphism Aj+1 → Aj. (iii) A specified subset of Σj gives cuts immediately before its letters. There are integers Bj, Tj ≥ 0 and a finite set of words Tj such that every nonzero word w of length at least Tj has the unique decomposition w = pw t1 · · · tr sw, |pw|, |sw| ≤ Bj, ti ∈ Tj. (2.1) Here pw precedes the first cut, sw begins at the last cut, and the ti are exactly the intervals between consecutive cuts. A cut is counted only if its following letter occurs in the word. For each t ∈ Tj there is a nonempty word ut over Σj+1 such that 1 ≤ |ut| ≤ k, |t| = Lj|ut|, [t] = [Ej(ut)] in Aj. (2.2)
